title: Fallback variants regression sweep and remediation plan for tokenizer/context/tooling gaps
creator: Priya Nair
description: Scope: Run a systematic regression sweep across our fallback model variants to identify tokenizer, context-length mapping, and tooling (function-calling / structured output / tool hooks) gaps that cause silent behavioral divergence when a request is routed from a primary model to a fallback. Deliverables: 1) a concrete list of incompatibility classes (tokenization shifts, truncated instruction context, missing tool signatures, structured output schema drift), 2) regression tests that reproduce failures end-to-end, 3) remediation plans for highest-risk gaps (>= medium customer impact), 4) a lightweight compatibility manifest format and a periodic verification job to keep manifests current. This ticket coordinates runtime tests, PRs to model onboarding metadata, and console/route-level flags that enable stricter fallback constraints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible test suite (CI job) that runs representative prompts through primary->fallback routes and flags differences in tokenization boundaries, truncated contexts, and tool-call failures. 2) A prioritized remediation list with owners and PRs for top-3 high-impact incompatibilities. 3) A compatibility manifest proposal committed to git (models/compat-manifests/) and a CI check that validates manifests in PRs. 4) Documentation page in Confluence with runbook for on-call and SEs describing how to interpret compatibility flags.
checklist: Inventory current fallback pairs and their metadata sources (model catalog + runtime mappings)
Define a canonical prompt corpus representing LLM features we rely on (tool-calls, function schemas, long-context vs prefix caching patterns)
Build tokenizer-diff harness (byte-level token alignment + mismatched token offsets report)
Add context-capacity tests that assert semantic-preservation for edge truncation cases (prefix-heavy prompts)
Exercise tool-calling and structured-output schemas end-to-end: primary model -> fallback -> tool executor simulator
Run sweep on sample of customer traffic (anonymized) behind feature flag to surface real-world edge cases
Draft compatibility manifest schema and add validation in model onboarding pipeline
Open remediation PRs for model metadata, runtime mapping changes, and console flags
Add periodic verification job to CI and schedule weekly results to routing team dashboard
notes: Initial hypothesis: most silent regressions stem from 3 sources: tokenizer drift between model families, implicit prompt truncation differences when switching context windows, and missing tool schemas in fallback variants.
We should avoid blocking launch of routes; instead add route-level controls: 'strict_parity' (failover blocked) and 'best_effort' (allow fallback with warning). Console needs a toggle per route.
Related doc: Confluence proposal - Fallback Variant Manifest: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Fallback+Variant+Manifest
SE follow-up: Coordinate with Solutions Eng (cc: Maya Singh) to run the sweep on 3 customer sandboxes next week
Risk: false positives from tokenizer-diff for models using different BPE vocabularies; tests must correlate token diffs to semantic drift checks (LM scoring similarity).
